question.text: In commodity markets, the term backwardation refers to:

answer.text: Futures price being higher than spot price
Futures price being lower than spot price
All prices moving in the same direction

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XV (p.76), backwardation is the condition where the futures price is lower than the spot price. In such a market, participants may expect the spot price to come down going forward. The Trap: Per p.75, contango is the opposite — futures price higher than spot price. Candidates often invert these two terms. The other distractors are unrelated to the spot-vs-futures relationship. Note: The directional definition (futures < spot) is what the source establishes; the source does not attribute backwardation specifically to tight supply, supply disruption, or strong immediate demand.
